newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bank shares seen down if no deals-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bank shares seen down if no deals-analysts.

text.p: Shares in Swedish banks, especially Nordbanken and S-E-Banken, are teetering on the verge of a sharp drop if a long-awaited merger or deal does not emerge soon, analysts said on Thursday.

"If there is no news at all, Nordbanken and S-E-Banken shares could underperform the general index from today and over a few months time, making the merger premium disappear," Fredrik Myren, analyst at HSBC James Capel, said.
Market players have been intent on a merger between Nordbanken and S-E-Banken as well as between Swedbank and Foreningsbanken.
But as time goes by and nothing happens, investors are beginning to fret.
"Already today you can see indications that there will not be any merger between S-E-Banken and Nordbanken are depressing share prices," one analyst said.

Business daily Finanstidningen on Thursday said the government was expected to offer its 59 percent Nordbanken stake to investors, rather than to Investor AB, the key holding company of Sweden's powerful Wallenberg family.
"Although interest rates are lower, (interest-sensitive) banking shares, including Nordbanken, are falling because of the newspaper article," it said
Nordbanken declined comment on the Finanstidningen article and no one at the Finance Ministry could be reached for comment.

The report contrasted with a January 3 article in the newspaper Dagens Industri, which said the government was likely to sell at least part of its stake to Investor, paving the way for a merger between Nordbanken and S-E-Banken, in which the Wallenbergs hold 15 percent.
The bank sector share index closed 1.46 percent lower on Thursday, with Nordbanken down five crowns at 220 and S-E-Banken one crown lower at 70. The general index ended up 0.27 percent.
One analyst said that if merger expectations faded, S-E-Banken's share price could slide by as much as 15 percent and Nordbanken's stock by around 10 percent.
"If you believe in a merger, you should stick to your Nordbanken shares. If not, there are other bank shares that are stronger," an analyst said.
"Handelsbanken is the bank share with the most potential after its acquisition of (mortgage lender) Stadshypotek," he said.
Handelsbanken bid around 23 billion crowns ($3.3 billion) for Stadshypotek in late 1996 and the bid is expected to be finalised in early 1997.
Banking shares have been riding on sector restructuring speculation since the autumn of 1996 and Nordbanken shares have surged on speculation about a merger between it and S-E-Banken.
Many analysts still believe in a merger, although they say that there are many obstacles, such as the banks having different aims and clashing cultures.
While Nordbanken focuses on private customers, municipalities and small companies, S-E-Banken is more of a risk-taker and is involved in large company deals, investment banking and corporate finance.
"Nordbanken and S-E-Banken are not such a good fit," an analyst said. "But there is a risk that they will merge." ($1=6.983 Swedish Crown)
